title: Achieving net zero
titleChinese: 气候变化挑战下如何实现“净零排放”
paragraphs: We are all aware of the effect greenhouse gas emissions is having on our planet and the efforts needed to tackle climate change. Most of us are doing our bit to minimise our impact on the environment, but despite our collective effort, are we doing enough to achieve net zero by 2050?

Net zero means not adding to the amount of greenhouse gases in the atmosphere. Many countries are doing their bit by changing how they generate and use power, thereby cutting carbon dioxide output. And they announced what further steps they were going to take at the recent COP26 summit in Glasgow.

In the UK, the government has been setting out its plans to achieve net zero by 2050. It’s recently announced an end date for the sale of gas boilers, which are used for heating homes. The idea is to replace them with heat pumps. It’s offering homeowners grants of up to £5,000 to get them installed. Another initiative in the UK is a big push towards electric vehicles. There are to be financial incentives for car manufacturers, and more charging points are to be installed in streets. And there’s to be a ban on the sale of new petrol and diesel cars by 2030.

But not all emissions can be reduced to zero, so those remaining will have to be compensated for, or offset. One way to do this is to plant thousands of trees, which are good at absorbing carbon dioxide. The UK government has pledged to plant 30,000 hectares of trees a year by 2025. There are other ideas too, but what’s certain is this will cost money. The CBI’s Tom Thackray told the BBC that “those costs have to be weighed up against the cost of inaction.”

Whether the UK, or anyone else, reaches net zero remains to be seen. And there’s some doubt about how this can be accurately measured anyway. But it’s generally recognised that a global effort is needed to tackle climate change. Therefore, net zero targets only make sense if every other country is moving in the same direction.

vocabulary.entry: greenhouse gas emission /ˈɡriːnhaʊs ɡæs iˈmɪʃn/ n. 温室气体排放
vocabulary.example: Greenhouse gas emission is closely linked to global temperature rise.
vocabulary.translation: 温室气体排放与全球气温上升密切相关。

vocabulary.entry: net zero /net ˈzɪərəʊ/ n. 净零排放
vocabulary.example: Net zero is a key goal for many countries' environmental policies.
vocabulary.translation: 净零排放是许多国家环境政策的核心目标。

vocabulary.entry: climate change /ˈklaɪmət tʃeɪndʒ/ n. 气候变化
vocabulary.example: Climate change has led to more frequent extreme weather events.
vocabulary.translation: 气候变化导致极端天气事件愈发频繁。

vocabulary.entry: carbon dioxide /ˈkɑːbən daɪˈɒksaɪd/ n. 二氧化碳
vocabulary.example: Carbon dioxide is one of the main greenhouse gases.
vocabulary.translation: 二氧化碳是主要的温室气体之一。

vocabulary.entry: COP26 summit /ˌsiː əʊ ˈpiː ˈtwenti sɪks ˈsʌmɪt/ n. 第26届联合国气候变化大会
vocabulary.example: The COP26 summit focused on global cooperation to cut emissions.
vocabulary.translation: 第26届联合国气候变化大会聚焦于全球减排合作。

vocabulary.entry: gas boiler /ɡæs ˈbɔɪlə(r)/ n. 燃气锅炉
vocabulary.example: The old gas boiler in my house is inefficient and polluting.
vocabulary.translation: 我家那台旧燃气锅炉效率低且污染环境。

vocabulary.entry: heat pump /hiːt pʌmp/ n. 热泵
vocabulary.example: A heat pump can transfer heat from the air to warm a house.
vocabulary.translation: 热泵可以从空气中提取热量为房屋供暖。

vocabulary.entry: grant /ɡrɑːnt/ n. 补贴；补助金
vocabulary.example: The government provides a grant for energy-efficient home improvements.
vocabulary.translation: 政府为高效节能的家居改造项目提供补贴。

vocabulary.entry: initiative /ɪˈnɪʃətɪv/ n. 举措；倡议
vocabulary.example: The new initiative aims to promote the use of renewable energy.
vocabulary.translation: 这项新举措旨在推广可再生能源的使用。

vocabulary.entry: electric vehicle /ɪˈlektrɪk ˈviːəkl/ n. 电动汽车
vocabulary.example: More and more people are choosing to buy an electric vehicle.
vocabulary.translation: 越来越多的人选择购买电动汽车。

vocabulary.entry: financial incentive /faɪˈnænʃl ɪnˈsentɪv/ n. 经济激励
vocabulary.example: The financial incentive has encouraged more manufacturers to produce green products.
vocabulary.translation: 这项经济激励政策鼓励了更多厂商生产绿色产品。

vocabulary.entry: charging point /ˈtʃɑːdʒɪŋ pɔɪnt/ n. 充电桩
vocabulary.example: I need to find a charging point to recharge my electric car.
vocabulary.translation: 我需要找一个充电桩给我的电动汽车充电。

vocabulary.entry: petrol car /ˈpetrəl kɑː(r)/ n. 汽油车
vocabulary.example: The sale of new petrol cars will be banned in the country by 2030.
vocabulary.translation: 该国将于2030年起禁止销售新的汽油车。

vocabulary.entry: diesel car /ˈdiːzl kɑː(r)/ n. 柴油车
vocabulary.example: Diesel cars are known for their higher fuel efficiency but more emissions.
vocabulary.translation: 柴油车以燃油效率较高但排放量更大而闻名。

vocabulary.entry: offset /ˈɒfset/ v. 抵消（排放量）
vocabulary.example: We can offset our carbon footprint by planting trees.
vocabulary.translation: 我们可以通过植树来抵消自己的碳足迹。

vocabulary.entry: hectare /ˈhekteə(r)/ n. 公顷
vocabulary.example: The forest covers an area of 500 hectares.
vocabulary.translation: 这片森林的面积达500公顷。

vocabulary.entry: pledge /pledʒ/ v. 承诺；保证
vocabulary.example: The company has pledged to reduce its emissions by 50% by 2030.
vocabulary.translation: 该公司承诺到2030年将排放量减少50%。

vocabulary.entry: weigh up /weɪ ʌp/ v. 权衡；考量
vocabulary.example: We need to weigh up the pros and cons before making a decision.
vocabulary.translation: 做决定前，我们需要权衡利弊。

vocabulary.entry: inaction /ɪnˈækʃn/ n. 不作为；无行动
vocabulary.example: Inaction on climate change will lead to severe consequences.
vocabulary.translation: 在气候变化问题上的不作为将导致严重后果。

vocabulary.entry: renewable energy /rɪˈnjuːəbl ˈenədʒi/ n. 可再生能源
vocabulary.example: Solar and wind power are two common types of renewable energy.
vocabulary.translation: 太阳能和风能是两种常见的可再生能源。

vocabulary.entry: carbon footprint /ˈkɑːbən ˈfʊtprɪnt/ n. 碳足迹
vocabulary.example: We should try to reduce our carbon footprint by saving energy.
vocabulary.translation: 我们应该通过节约能源来减少自己的碳足迹。

vocabulary.entry: extreme weather event /ɪkˈstriːm ˈweðə ɪˈvent/ n. 极端天气事件
vocabulary.example: Hurricanes and droughts are examples of extreme weather events.
vocabulary.translation: 飓风和干旱都属于极端天气事件。

vocabulary.entry: environmental policy /ɪnˌvaɪrənˈmentl ˈpɒləsi/ n. 环境政策
vocabulary.example: The government's new environmental policy has received widespread support.
vocabulary.translation: 政府的新环境政策获得了广泛支持。

vocabulary.entry: energy efficiency /ˈenədʒi ɪˈfɪʃnsi/ n. 能源效率
vocabulary.example: Improving energy efficiency is an effective way to cut emissions.
vocabulary.translation: 提高能源效率是减排的有效途径。

vocabulary.entry: global cooperation /ˈɡləʊbl kəʊˌɒpəˈreɪʃn/ n. 全球合作
vocabulary.example: Global cooperation is essential to address climate change.
vocabulary.translation: 全球合作对于应对气候变化至关重要。

sentences.english: We are all aware of the effect greenhouse gas emissions is having on our planet and the efforts needed to tackle climate change.
sentences.chinese: 我们都清楚温室气体排放对地球造成的影响，也明白应对气候变化需要付出怎样的努力。

sentences.english: Most of us are doing our bit to minimise our impact on the environment, but despite our collective effort, are we doing enough to achieve net zero by 2050?
sentences.chinese: 大多数人都在尽自己的一份力，减少对环境的影响，但即便我们共同努力，要在2050年实现净零排放目标，我们目前所做的真的足够吗？

sentences.english: Net zero means not adding to the amount of greenhouse gases in the atmosphere.
sentences.chinese: 净零排放是指不再向大气中新增温室气体。

sentences.english: Many countries are doing their bit by changing how they generate and use power, thereby cutting carbon dioxide output.
sentences.chinese: 许多国家正通过改变能源的生产和使用方式来尽一份力，从而减少二氧化碳的排放量。

sentences.english: And they announced what further steps they were going to take at the recent COP26 summit in Glasgow.
sentences.chinese: 在最近于格拉斯哥举办的第26届联合国气候变化大会上，各国公布了后续将要采取的举措。

sentences.english: In the UK, the government has been setting out its plans to achieve net zero by 2050.
sentences.chinese: 英国政府已出台了2050年实现净零排放的相关计划。

sentences.english: It’s recently announced an end date for the sale of gas boilers, which are used for heating homes. The idea is to replace them with heat pumps. It’s offering homeowners grants of up to £5,000 to get them installed.
sentences.chinese: 该国近期宣布了家用燃气锅炉的截止销售时间，计划用热泵取而代之，同时还向房主提供最高5000英镑的补贴，用于安装热泵。

sentences.english: Another initiative in the UK is a big push towards electric vehicles. There are to be financial incentives for car manufacturers, and more charging points are to be installed in streets. And there’s to be a ban on the sale of new petrol and diesel cars by 2030.
sentences.chinese: 英国的另一项举措是大力推广电动汽车，不仅为汽车制造商提供财务补贴，还将在街道上增设更多充电桩，并且计划在2030年起禁止销售新的汽油车和柴油车。

sentences.english: But not all emissions can be reduced to zero, so those remaining will have to be compensated for, or offset.
sentences.chinese: 但并非所有排放都能降至零，因此剩余的排放量必须通过抵消手段来处理。

sentences.english: One way to do this is to plant thousands of trees, which are good at absorbing carbon dioxide.
sentences.chinese: 其中一种方法是大规模植树造林，树木善于吸收二氧化碳。

sentences.english: The UK government has pledged to plant 30,000 hectares of trees a year by 2025.
sentences.chinese: 英国政府承诺，到2025年每年将植树3万公顷。

sentences.english: There are other ideas too, but what’s certain is this will cost money.
sentences.chinese: 当然还有其他的减排思路，但可以肯定的是，实现净零排放需要投入大量资金。

sentences.english: The CBI’s Tom Thackray told the BBC that “those costs have to be weighed up against the cost of inaction.”
sentences.chinese: 英国工业联合会的汤姆·撒克雷在接受BBC采访时表示：“我们必须权衡这些投入与不作为所付出的代价。”

sentences.english: Whether the UK, or anyone else, reaches net zero remains to be seen.
sentences.chinese: 英国或其他任何国家能否如期实现净零排放，尚有待观察。

sentences.english: And there’s some doubt about how this can be accurately measured anyway.
sentences.chinese: 此外，关于如何准确测算净零排放，目前也存在一些争议。

sentences.english: But it’s generally recognised that a global effort is needed to tackle climate change.
sentences.chinese: 但人们普遍认为，应对气候变化需要全球共同努力。

sentences.english: Therefore, net zero targets only make sense if every other country is moving in the same direction.
sentences.chinese: 因此，只有当所有国家都朝着同一个方向迈进时，净零排放目标才有实际意义。
